Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. I have seven picks I like this week, including player props on Patrick Mahomes , Drake Maye , and Tony Pollard , plus three spreads picks for the 1 PM Eastern games. Best of luck, happy November, and enjoy your day! Vikings at Lions (-3): O/U 46.5 I said Monday of this week on NBC that this was the no-brainer of the week. It’s a miracle that the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the NFL, and to me, they are the most overrated team. In the last four games, Minnesota has beaten Tampa Bay, Miami, New Orleans, and Indianapolis; those teams are a combined 7-20. Last season, the Vikings swept the Lions in the regular season, and adding Kyler Murray likely doesn’t equate to another sweep over Detroit. Murray ranks 21st and 26th in passer rating against man and zone coverage, 28th in blitzed completion percentage (54.8%), and 26th in play-action completion percentage (54.9%). On early downs, Minnesota ranks in success rate, while Detroit is first. Going score for score on the road as an underdog with Jared Goff and the Lions doesn’t seem plausible to me. I like Detroit -3 at -120 odds. Pick: Lions -3 (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Titans at Bengals (-12.5): O/U 46.5 Tony Pollard had a season-high 129 rushing yards on 25 carries and tied a career-high with three rushing touchdowns. It was a great day for Pollard, but the Titans lost at the buzzer 27-24 to the Browns. Now, Tennessee goes on the road as double-digit underdogs in Cincinnati. Not a recipe for success. Last week, Pollard had an amazing game script to be fed, maybe the best he’s had all year, but I don’t see it this week, especially going up against Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen . The Bengals held Derrick Henry to 45 rushing yards on 17 carries last week, and with Cam Ward striking no fear in the Bengals’ hearts, I’d think Cincy stacks the box and attempt to take Pollard out of the equation. I went Under 65.5 rushing yards on Pollard and would go down to 60.5. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 65.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Browns at Steelers (-3.5): O/U 38.5 I still can’t believe my eyes and ears regarding the Cleveland Browns being 5-2! But all good things must come to an end, right? All five of Cleveland’s wins have come by four or fewer points, and they needed a walkoff field goal to beat the Titans in Tennessee and the same at home against the Ravens in the last two weeks. Cleveland has been playing with fire recently, while the Steelers were spotted flying back from Paris playing with ice. Aaron Rodgers was wearing chains that cost more than my house and probably yours too on that flight back from the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris. Rodgers said it was his favorite road flight of his lengthy NFL career, and the Steelers are starting to hit their stride with three-straight wins following the loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers traveling back to an immediate game is worrisome because the last eight teams that played in London, then a game in the States the following week, went 0-8 ATS! However, the Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. It’s a revenge spot for Pittsburgh, and if you’ve seen the back-and-forth between Cam Heyward and Jared Verse this week, then you know it’s going to be a classic AFC North slugfest. Give me Pittsburgh at home -3.5. I’d prefer a -3, but the sportsbooks are playing more defense than ever this season. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (1 unit) Falcons at Bucs (-2.5): O/U Tampa Bay got that Baker bump last week! Baker Mayfield came back from injury and Tampa Bay looked inspired. The Bucs rattled Bryce Young last week and destroyed his confidence turning three turnovers into 17 of the teams 43 points. This week won’t be so easy hosting Atlanta in a letdown spot off the hype. Mayfield only threw the ball 11 times, so we truly don’t know how healthy he is or how effective he will be, but we know what to expect from Atlanta. The Falcons have the fifth-best offensive success rate since Michael Penix has taken over, and he’s gotten the ball out quick with 50% of his passes coming within 2.5 seconds (fourth-best). That could be the key against a blitz and pressure heavy Bucs defense. Tampa Bay loads the box with eight or more players at the second-highest clip (22.1%) and blitzes 40.4% of the time when doing so, which ranks fifth-most. I’d expect a lot of screens, draws, and quick throws to offeset the Bucs defense, while Atlanta likely brings pressure and tries to hit Mayfield as many times as possible to truly test his health and conditioning. Give me Atlanta. Pick: Falcons +2.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Patriots (-7) at Dolphins: O/U 43.5 Last season, Drake Maye completed 33-of-41 (80.5%) passes for 421 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions over two wins against Miami. Maye even added 72 rushing yards and another score on 15 carries in those two outings. This Miami defense is even less menacing than last year. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, and two came in Week 1 against Kirk Cousins , with another last week courtesy of Geno Smith . When Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes , Brock Purdy , and Kyler Murray played Miami, that group averaged 242.5 passing yards against the Dolphins and combined for eight touchdown passes to one interception. Kyler Murray was the only quarterback who hasn’t thrown at least two touchdowns against Miami. At -102 odds, I like Maye to go Under 0.5 Interceptions versus Miami for a third consecutive time and like 2+ Pass touchdowns for parlays. Pick: Drake Maye Under 0.5 Interceptions (1 unit) Chiefs (-1.5) at Broncos: O/U 40.5 In Week 1 against Denver, Patrick Mahomes came back from a major surgery and finished with 184 passing yards, 15-of-27 passing, and three total touchdowns, including an epic rushing score to start the game. He went Under all of his props except passing touchdowns and rushing yards. Fast forward to last week, Mahomes had his worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks in Seattle. Mahomes turns around and goes to Denver to face a Broncos defense that almost went to the Super Bowl. It’s going to be a long day for the Chiefs, but unless Kenneth Walker goes crazy again (191 total yards, 2 TDs) this looks like a spot for Mahomes to go over his props. The Broncos average 5.1 plays per possession, ranking worst in the NFL. That’s one area that points toward more plays and possessions for the Chiefs. Both of these teams rarely allow sacks or turn the ball over, so we should see plenty of possessions. Both teams had 12 drives in Week 1’s meeting, and Kansas City ran 20 more plays than Denver (62-42) thanks to the running game, and it was Davis Webb ‘s first game as an OC with the Broncos. Still, Kansas City will likely run more plays and have more possessions than Denver. Denver got back Jonathan Cooper last week, plus Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga could both play today. The Denver defense has usually limited the touchdown damage through the air from Mahomes, but in order to move the ball against Denver’s defense, Mahomes will have to be actively taking what the Broncos can give him. I like Mahomes to go Over 20.5 completions and 220.5 paassing yards up to 21.5 and 225.5. I lean his Over pass attempts. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. Here are my best bets for the Sunday and Monday slate in the NFL Week 9. Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings. Best of luck! Bengals (-3.5) vs Falcons: O/U 52.5 The Bengals and Falcons kick off in Madrid, Spain, at 9:30 AM Eastern Sunday morning, so set your alarm clocks, aka your phones! This should be a fantastic matchup, and I am looking at the Atlanta offense for a bounce-back spot. Last week against Tampa Bay, the Falcons lost in a monsoon as Michael Penix threw four interceptions, while the Atlanta defense was run. In sunny weather, we should expect the Falcons to look night and day. The Bengals are on a three-game winning streak over Miami, Baltimore, and Tennessee. Cam Ward threw for 304 yards and touchdowns, plus Tony Pollard ran for 117 yards and two scores on the Bengals. The Bengals’ four wins all come against teams with losing records so far, while the Falcons have shown their potential with wins over Green Bay and San Francisco. I still think the Falcons have the highest ceiling in the NFC South. I’ll take the +3.5 down to +3. Pick: Falcons +3.5 (1 unit) Giants (-3) at Eagles: O/U 38.5 For the first time since November 1, 2009, the New York Giants are favorites in Philadelphia, and that’s no mistake. Things are so bad during the Eagles’ six-game losing streak that they’ve benched Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton . Philadelphia has a bye week up next, so this is them 100-percent trying to see what they have before they decide on their intentions in the second half of the season. If the Eagles lose this game, they are borderline out of the postseason before Week 11 starts, but that desperation doesn’t interest me because they haven’t had any rhythm amid all the injuries. The Giants, on the other hand, are in first place in the division, coming out of a bye week after an impressive 27-21 OT win over Houston. New York has found something with J.J. McCarthy , and if Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers are bought in like they were against Houston (232 combined yards), then so am I. I like the Giants -3. Pick: Giants -3 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Packers at Patriots (-3): O/U 44.5 Green Bay has averaged a league-high 81.7% of their yards through the air, and 65.7% of their plays are passes. At some point, regression has to hit, and the backfield becomes more reliable. Josh Jacobs has started to turn the wheels of regression, but as we’ve seen through two games, it may take time. This matchup will be interesting since New England runs the third-most man coverage (29%). Love has completed 51% of his passes against man (25th) for 6.2 yards per attempt (6.2). Love’s faced a slew of bad defenses this season, and New England certainly isn’t bad. Christian Watson is a go, so I expect plenty of passes, but 37.5 is still steep despite Love throwing 41-plus times in three straight. I am going to sell high on Love and also go under Matthew Golden ‘s 68.5 receiving yards. Last week, Watson was very active before he suffered an injury that opened the door for Golden to sneak over his yards prop. Golden has gone over his yards prop in three of his last four games and saw 12-plus targets in three straight. However, Golden ranks 66th in target separation versus man coverage, and going up Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III won’t be easy. I’m going under on both Love and Golden. JSN has been nothing short of spectacular. If the season ended today, he is the Offensive Player of the Year. JSN leads the league in receiving yards (985) and receiving touchdowns (9). He has four straight games with 100-plus receiving yards and seven out of eight on the season, but I am going Under. Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett away and will roll with Gardner Minshew for the meantime. Sam Darnold is out for Seattle, so Drew Lock will step up. Luckily for Lock, Seattle’s backfield is more crowded than ever and willing to assist. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet both returned in the last two weeks, plus George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson are capable backs. Arizona has lost 10 straight to Seattle, and after selling this past week, I could see the Seahawks rolling and working on their ground game. In Week 2 against Arizona with Lock at quarterback, Seattle ran the ball 40 times and threw it 26. JSN caught 155 of Lock’s 235 yards (11 targets). Ridiculous, but we could see a similar result here in play calling, capping JSN’s production. Pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Under 94.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Buccaneers at Bears (-6): O/U 47.5 Baker Mayfield has had the easiest job in the NFL over the last two weeks. Mayfield has thrown 14 passes in past two games. Against Atlanta, Mayfield and the Bucs became the first quarterback/team to not complete a pass since September 29, 1974! Mayfield went 0-for-3 and we might not see that feat happen for another 50 years. However, the good days are over. Welcome to the end times, Baker. You are in Chicago facing a white-hot Bears team with additions on the defense from trades and guys returning from injury. Mayfield won’t have the liberty of handing the ball to his talented backs like he has literally over 100 times in the last two games. I like all of Mayfield’s Overs this week, but my favorites are the attempts. Chicago leads the NFL in time of possession margin, so Mayfield will have to make his possessions count, and the Bears allow big plays through the air, so I’d expect Mayfield to take some shots downfield. Pick: Baker Mayfield Over 29.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Bills (-3) at Vikings: O/U 43.5 Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings as Kyler Murray deals with an injured hamstring. Minnesota is coming off their first loss of the season, 19-15 to the Lions. Buffalo was off a bye for a hyped up game against Baltimore, but due to two quarterback injuries, the Bills ended up routing the Ravens 36-10 in a game Buffalo never trailed. Buffalo gets two backup quarterbacks back-to-back weeks as they go for their fourth-straight win. I like the chances that happen. Buffalo leads the NFL in points per drive (3.07), and Minnesota is first in points allowed per drive (1.18). The Bills have been involved in the highest-scoring games and the Vikings the fewest. It’s a clash of offense versus defense, but I think offense will win. Minnesota has allowed two passing touchdowns since Week 2, but they’ve played Baker Mayfield , Malik Willis , Tyler Shough , Daniel Jones , and then Jared Goff last week. Josh Allen is on a different planet than those guys. I will gladly take Buffalo -3. I’d go out to -5.5. My Week 5 betting card finished 7-4 (4-2 on sides/totals and 3-2 on player props), marking five straight weeks in the black. Over five weeks, the official plays went 7-4, 6-5, 6-4, 6-5 and 7-4. We are 32-22 overall for a strong 59% hit rate. The best of the bunch was the Packers as home underdogs against the Bears. I called that one a lock, and Green Bay won outright, 31-7. Divisional home underdogs? Trust the process. The Steelers laying a field goal and the Bills Moneyline in overtime against the Rams cashed, too. I was kicking myself for not making the Steelers a top pick on the Best Bets Show ahead of Week 5 - given that Indianapolis was coming off an international game and had no bye week. The one that stung was the Eagles-Jaguars spread: Jacksonville won, but only by two points. But I survived my back-to-back double-header wedding weekend (again, congrats to my sister, Rachael, and new big brother-in-law Matt, and my close friends, Mollie and Mike). Let's get back to business with all remaining games for Week 16 featured below (including the Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football matchups). More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> Two things stand out in the league-wide trends heading into Week 6. First, prime-time underdogs have covered nine straight games, and all nine won outright. Tampa Bay, Baltimore and Buffalo kept it going last week. Dallas-Green Bay on Sunday night and Washington-San Francisco on Monday night are the next tests. Second, the home-underdog edge cooled off slightly. After starting the season 14-8-1 ATS, home underdogs went just 1-4-1 in Week 5 and sit at 15-12-2 against the spread (ATS) for the season, a bit under 56% of decided bets. They still have won 12 out of 29 games outright (41%). Divisional home underdogs are still the sweet spot at 6-2 ATS (5-3 straight up). Based on the early lines, the Week 6 slate has home underdogs in the Buccaneers (vs. Steelers), Browns (vs. Ravens, in-division), Giants (vs. Saints), Falcons (vs. Bears) and Raiders (vs. Bills), and possibly the Packers if the Cowboys stay favored. The Browns-Ravens game is the only divisional game of the group. A reminder that Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on bye, so we have 14 games this week, excluding Thursday’s Seahawks-Broncos matchup. We took the Seahawks laying less than a field goal. And it hit, despite Bo Nix’s horrific performance; Seattle fell short in overtime in Denver. After Week 6, prime-time underdogs have covered in 10 straight games, and all 10 won outright. Pretty crazy. League-Wide Trends Week 5 Recap Favorites went 7-7-1 ATS; underdogs went 7-7-1 ATS (15 games). Home teams went 4-9-1 ATS; road teams went 9-4-1 ATS (one neutral-site game excluded). Overall O/U: 39-40. Home Underdogs (through Week 5) Home underdogs are 15-12-2 ATS (29 games; neutral-site games excluded), which is 55.6% of decided bets. Home underdogs have won 12 of those 29 games outright (41%), and the OVER went 14-15. Divisional home underdogs are 6-2 ATS (5-3 straight up); all divisional underdogs are 14-4 ATS (18 games). Home teams went 8-6-1 ATS; road teams went 6-8-1 ATS (one neutral-site game excluded). Overall O/U: 9-7. Streaks: Prime-time underdogs have covered in nine straight games (and won all nine outright, dating back to Falcons-Packers in Week 3). Prime-time home teams have failed to cover in four straight. The OVER has hit in the last two prime-time games. Arizona is 2-0 ATS in 2026 when getting eight or more points. The risk is that Arizona has lost by 24 twice (Weeks 2 and 5) and allows 32.4 points per game. Woof . It’s scary because the Cardinals are willing to drop back and throw 40 to 45 times per game with a combination of Jacoby Brissett/Michael Wilson/Trey McBride, and that creates garbage-time opportunities. I like the value with Arizona at this number. Arizona’s biggest cover this season came in Week 1 at the Chargers in Los Angeles, where the Cardinals were 9.5-point underdogs and won outright, and I’ll take them playing in Los Angeles again. This is also one of those classic “close your eyes” specials: Team gets blown out by 21+ points one week, then catches double-digit points the following week, etc. This matchup doesn’t align with the official “close your eyes” special (21 points versus the spread, so technically the Raiders qualify this week after getting blown out by New England), but you catch my drift. Even so… The Cardinals got blown out twice last year by the Rams, 37-20 and 45-17, but I think we can all agree that last year’s Rams team might be better than the 2026 version. L.A. covered the double-digit spread in both games, although Arizona was winning late into the third quarter in the second matchup. If you can’t stomach the Cardinals, the over is another option. Four of the last five games between these two teams have gone over the closing line total. Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Over 53.5 Points Trends As a road favorite (the role it plays here), Buffalo is 1-0 ATS (100%) and 1-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all road games, 2-0 ATS and 2-0 O/U; across all games as a favorite, 3-1 ATS and 3-1 O/U; across all 2026 games, 4-1 ATS and 4-1 O/U. As a home underdog (the role it plays here), Las Vegas is 1-0 ATS (100%) and 1-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all home games, 2-0 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all games as an underdog, 3-1 ATS and 3-1 O/U; across all 2026 games, 4-1 ATS and 3-2 O/U. Buffalo streaks through Week 5: 4-1 straight up (one-game win streak), 4-1 against the spread (one-game cover streak), 4-1 toward the total (two-game Over streak). Las Vegas streaks through Week 5: 3-2 straight up (two-game losing streak), 4-1 against the spread (one-game non-cover streak), 3-2 toward the total (three-game Over streak). Buffalo comes in off a 37-34 road win at the Rams as a 3.5-point underdog, covering (Week 5). Las Vegas comes in off a 45-17 road loss at New England as a 3.5-point underdog, failing to cover (Week 5). Josh Allen is 24-16-2 ATS in his career (60%) after the Week 5 cover at the Rams (23-16-2 entering the week), and has an 8-1 career record in domes. Buffalo is averaging 32.8 points per game in 2026 (164 points in five games). Buffalo is 4-2 ATS and 5-1 O/U over its last six games (2025 Divisional Round through 2026 Week 5); Las Vegas is 5-1 ATS and 3-3 O/U over its last six games (2025 Week 18 through 2026 Week 5). Injuries #Raiders DT Tonka Hemingway (concussion) is the only player not seen at practice. WR Jalen Nailor is no longer wearing a red non-contact jersey. — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) October 16, 2026 Thursday injury report pic.twitter.com/9n3U6lo1ER — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 15, 2026 Betting Preview I like the Over. The Raiders’ loss to the Patriots said more about the Patriots than the Raiders. Las Vegas is very boom-or-bust on defense, and when its pressure doesn’t get home, it gives up explosive downfield plays. Drake Maye had plenty of time to throw, even after Will Campbell got hurt. When you play the Buffalo Bills, saddle up, as there are going to be a lot of explosive plays. Josh Allen indoors is a rare occurrence, and I expect it to remind us how much fun he is on fast turf with all of these playmakers. Buffalo games average 61.0 combined points and are 4-1 to the Over. Las Vegas games average 52.2, and the Raiders are on a three-game Over streak. Seth Woolcock dropped this as one of his best bets for Week 6, riding the over in Sin City. I tend to agree, given that these high-total games have not closed high enough so far this season. Through Week 5, games with a closing total of 50+ points are 7-2 to the Over (78%). Dropping the cutoff to 49.5 makes it 9-2 across 11 games. NFL Sunday Night Football Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Cowboys Moneyline Trends As a road underdog (the role it plays here), Dallas is 1-0 ATS (100%) and 1-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all road games, 1-1 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all games as an underdog, 1-0-1 ATS and 2-0 O/U; across all 2026 games, 2-2-1 ATS and 3-2 O/U. As a home favorite (the role it plays here), Green Bay is 0-1 ATS (0%) and 1-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all home games, 1-1 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all games as a favorite, 0-2-1 ATS and 1-2 O/U; across all 2026 games, 1-3-1 ATS and 2-3 O/U. Dallas streaks through Week 5: 2-3 straight up (one-game losing streak), 2-2-1 against the spread (one-game non-cover streak), 3-2 toward the total (one-game Under streak). Green Bay streaks through Week 5: 3-2 straight up (two-game win streak), 1-3-1 against the spread (one-game cover streak), 2-3 toward the total (two-game Under streak). Dallas comes in off a 24-16 home loss to Tampa Bay as an 8.5-point favorite, failing to cover (Week 5). Green Bay comes in off a 31-7 home win over Chicago as a 1.5-point underdog, covering (Week 5). Green Bay ended a 0-9-1 ATS skid (10 straight games without a cover) in Week 5, a 31-7 win over Chicago as a 1.5-point home underdog. Green Bay is 5-11 ATS as a favorite since 2025 (the Week 4 game at Tampa Bay, a push at -3, is not counted). Dallas is 2-3-1 ATS and 3-3 O/U over its last six games (2025 Week 18 through 2026 Week 5); Green Bay is 1-4-1 ATS and 3-3 O/U over its last six games (2025 Wild Card Round through 2026 Week 5). Prime-time record in 2026 (through Week 5): Dallas is 0-2 ATS and 0-2 O/U in 2 prime-time games; Green Bay is 0-1 ATS and 1-0 O/U in 1 prime-time game. Injuries Brandon Cisse added to the injury report and is questionable. pic.twitter.com/ByPqPtKkwm — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 16, 2026 Betting Preview This has to be a shootout, right? The last time these teams met was a 40-40 tie on Sunday Night Football last year. In the last six games these teams have played, the total has gone Over. As for sides… I’ll take the team with the points, the Cowboys, as painful as that sounds after taking them to cover and win outright last week against the Buccaneers, and then watching them lose outright. In retrospect, why would I think they could cover that line? Anytime they are heavy favorites, you fade them to oblivion, and anytime they get written off as underdogs, that is when you want to be on their side. I also don’t think Green Bay has totally erased its issues. The offensive line is still really bad, and you saw the cracks up front at times against Jordan Love when the Bears’ pressure got home. When it didn’t, he was able to rip off explosive plays, which he will be able to do against Dallas too. It will be back-and-forth and come down to the last possession, so I’ll take the team catching the points with Dak Prescott as a slight underdog (7-2 ATS as an underdog since 2025, second-best mark in the NFL). Conversely, you never want to bet on the Packers as favorites in any capacity… they are 6-11 ATS as a favorite since last season (0-2-1 this season), fresh off their first cover in their last 10 games. Don’t let Week 5 change your entire outlook on both of these teams. Not to mention… the prime-time underdogs this season have covered 10 straight games, and won all of them outright. Back to the total briefly, because there’s a chance of some wind in the forecast that bettors should be wary of. Gusts up to 27 miles per hour (MPH) could be problematic, so be sure to do your due diligence before firing on the game total. And the full integration of Joey Porter Jr. could eventually turn the tide of the Dallas defense starting in Week 6. Meanwhile, Green Bay could be down another cornerback in Brandon Cisse. Christian Watson has scored the first touchdown in his last three home games with Jordan Love as his quarterback (Green Bay has scored the first touchdown in six straight games). That was Welsh’s favorite first touchdown call on our Week 6 Props Show. I already mentioned my first touchdown call, but I’m still interested in touchdown props for this game. Let me introduce Packers wide receiver J. Michael Sturdivant. He caught a 43-yard touchdown last week that was overturned on an offensive pass interference call. But the coaches acknowledged this week that it would have been awesome to get him his first touchdown, but that it will be coming pretty soon (S/O The Coachspeak Index). Props Christian Watson First Touchdown Scorer (+1000) J. Michael Sturdivant Anytime Touchdown Scorer (+1050) NFL Monday Night Football Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: 49ers -7.5 Trends As a road underdog (the role it plays here), Washington is 1-1 ATS (50%) and 2-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all road games, 1-1 ATS and 2-0 O/U; across all games as an underdog, 2-2 ATS and 3-1 O/U; across all 2026 games, 2-3 ATS and 4-1 O/U. As a home favorite (the role it plays here), San Francisco is 2-1 ATS (67%) and 2-1 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all home games, 2-1 ATS and 2-1 O/U; across all games as a favorite, 2-1 ATS and 2-1 O/U; across all 2026 games, 4-1 ATS and 3-2 O/U. Washington streaks through Week 5: 1-3-1 straight up (last game was a tie; no active win/loss streak), 2-3 against the spread (two-game non-cover streak), 4-1 toward the total (one-game Over streak). San Francisco streaks through Week 5: 5-0 straight up (five-game win streak), 4-1 against the spread (two-game cover streak), 3-2 toward the total (one-game Over streak). Washington comes in off a 27-27 tie with the Giants as a 3.5-point favorite, failing to cover (Week 5). San Francisco comes in off a 32-29 road win at Seattle as a 3-point underdog, covering (Week 5). San Francisco had gone Over the total in each of its previous five games as a favorite before the Week 4 game against Denver went Under (24-14, 38 points vs. 48.5). Washington is 3-3 ATS and 4-2 O/U over its last six games (2025 Week 18 through 2026 Week 5); San Francisco is 4-2 ATS and 4-2 O/U over its last six games (2025 Divisional Round through 2026 Week 5). Washington games are averaging 52.8 combined points in 2026 (264 in five games), and San Francisco games are averaging 49.4 (247 in five games). Prime-time record in 2026 (through Week 5): Washington has not played a prime-time game in 2026; San Francisco is 1-0 ATS and 0-1 O/U in 1 prime-time game. Injuries There's a growing possibility that the 49ers may be without Mike Evans & Nick Bosa vs the #Commanders pic.twitter.com/hNUbIL5LlG — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 16, 2026 Betting Preview Originally, I wanted to back the Commanders. Getting more than a touchdown with Jayden Daniels, a quarterback who performs well when his team is the underdog, is appealing, and he looked fantastic running the ball in his return last week versus the New York Giants (despite also taking five sacks). But this Washington defense is so bad that Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and whoever else is healthy are going to have a field day against it. The biggest difference in the 49ers’ defense is linebacker Fred Warner. Warner is the tide that lifts all boats, and he can spy Daniels as a runner, which is what concerns me about backing Washington. If he slows Daniels down on the ground, you are left needing Washington’s offense to pass its way back, and the Commanders can’t consistently run the ball behind a shaky offensive line that traveled cross-country after an overtime tie. I usually don’t like laying this many points with the 49ers, so in the early look this was a shy-away spot for me. But upon further research, the 49ers’ 10-3-1 mark ATS as a favorite ranks No. 1 in the NFL since 2025. It’s not as great at home (4-3-1), but positive nonetheless. San Francisco as a favorite is still a lean I like, and I’d rather be with the 49ers than the Commanders. It’s rare to see an injury report for a 49ers game when they look like the healthiest team. I’m treating it as a lean rather than a play at this number. My favorite play in this game is betting against the Commanders quarterback and his legs. The 49ers are allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game to quarterbacks, including mobile quarterbacks like Malik Willis and Bo Nix. They combined for 16 yards. No quarterback has rushed for more than 10 yards against the 49ers this season, with four out of five going Under their rushing projection. Willis had six rushing yards on a 37.5-yard rushing prop. Daniels has recorded 201 yards on scrambles this season, second-most in the NFL, and has averaged a league-leading 12.6 yards per carry on those runs (minimum five carries). The 49ers’ defense has faced five scrambles, tied for the fewest in the NFL, and has allowed 5.6 yards per carry on those runs (6th-fewest) according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That's where our Featured Pros come in. We asked a panel of sharp analysts to break down their favorite NFL Draft prop bets, highlighting where the value lies and which lines may be mispriced as draft buzz heats up. Whether you're targeting early-round chaos or late-round sleepers, these expert-backed picks can help you stay one step ahead on draft night. More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> Top NFL Draft Prop Bets (Odds courtesy of DraftKings SportsBook unless otherwise stated) What is your single favorite prop bet heading into the 2026 NFL Draft and why? Please include the odds with your selection. Rueben Bain Jr. to be a Top 10 pick: Yes ( -162 ) “Miami Hurricanes EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. has 30.9-inch arms, which likely cause him to slide, but I don't think he can get past eight overall to the New Orleans Saints or nine overall to the Kansas City Chiefs. The 21-year-old finished fifth in the ACC with 7.5 sacks as a freshman, before regressing somewhat as a sophomore while battling injuries. Bain Jr. then returned to form this past year, setting career-highs in tackles (54), tackles for loss (15.5), and sacks (9.5), while leading the Hurricanes to a College Football Playoff (CFP) National Championship appearance. This earned him AP Consensus All-America and ACC Defensive Player of the Year honors, as well as the Ted Hendricks Award. Those accomplishments, a high character, and elite film should be enough to keep him inside the top 10 picks, making this arguably the best prop bet available.” – Seth Woolcock ( FantasyPros ) Jacob Rodriguez drafted inside the top-32 ( +500 ) “I’m a sucker for the “Will this player be drafted in Round 1″ betting market. Right now, my favorite approach is to select Texas Tech LB Jacob Rodriguez inside the top-32 at 5-1 odds. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Jermod McCoy (Tennessee), Colton Hood (Tennessee), and Ty Simpson (Alabama) are better than 50/50 to go in the first round, but McCoy’s stock is plummeting due to a worrisome knee issue, and there are only two or three potential first-round suitors for Simpson, none of whom would draft him with the picks they currently hold in the top half of the round. If all of these SEC maybes make it, that’s seven, leaving one SEC player to spare. Chase Bisontis (Texas A&M), Cashius Howell (Texas A&M), Zion Young (Missouri), C.J. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile. While Jordyn Tyson is hands down the best pure receiver in this class, his extensive injury history, including major knee surgery and a broken collarbone, has dropped him to the second or third receiver off the board on most teams’ lists. NFL front offices are notoriously risk-averse in the top ten, making Tate the safer bet to anchor a professional offense immediately. This shift in draft stock highlights a classic case where reliability outweighs elite but fragile potential. Ultimately, taking Tate at these odds is a play on the certainty of his health and polished Buckeye pedigree over the medical gamble Tyson presents.” – Lawrence Iacona ( Gridiron Experts ) Makai Lemon to be first WR drafted ( +2000 ) “Makai Lemon – 1st Wide Receiver Drafted ( +2000 at Caesars ). I'm going with Makai Lemon as the first wide receiver off the board. Bold, absolutely. Crazy? Maybe, but hear me out. This is often a copycat league. I believe a wide receiver-needy team, such as the New York Giants, might consider Lemon. The Giants already have Malik Nabers, a top outside threat, and could look to replicate what Seattle did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit with Amon-Ra St. Brown, using Lemon in a similar role. The Seahawks’ stout defense has oddsmakers valuing them as a -3 betting favorite at home, while the point total sits at 46.5. We’re coming off a perfect 3-0 outing with my previous Week 7 edition of NFL Monday Night Football Player Props & Picks: Cowboys vs. Eagles . Dak Prescott finished with 3 passing touchdowns, going Over 1.5 Passing Touchdowns in the 1st half. Ryan Flournoy cashed Over 33.5 Receiving Yards with 4-70 on 4 targets, and CeeDee Lamb hauled in a 1st-quarter touchdown to cash his Anytime TD Scorer prop at +120 odds. Let’s keep building our bankroll and cashing tickets heading into tonight’s NFC tilt between the Bears and Seahawks. I’ve got 3 player props to target in multiple betting markets. Follow me on X @ Matt_MacKay for more NFL betting analysis and free picks. More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> Best NFL Monday Night Football Player Prop Bets – Week 8: Bears vs. Seahawks (Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook ) Sam Darnold 230+ Passing Yards ( -135 ) Sam Darnold looked like a reigning Super Bowl champion during his last outing against the Kansas City Chiefs, logging a 71 percent completion rate for over 250 yards. Tonight, Darnold gets Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back into the Seahawks’ backfield. This will set up play-action much more effectively, while facing a Bears defense that has allowed 310+ passing yards in 2 of its previous 3 appearances. Expect another big night between Darnold and star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold has recorded 230+ passing yards in 3 of his past 5 starts for Seattle. Oddsmakers have set his passing yards line at 237.5, so let’s lay a bit of juice and play Darnold’s passing yards line to 230+ at -135 odds. D’Andre Swift Under 59.5 Rushing Yards ( -115 ) The Bears continue to funnel carries to D’Andre Swift. However, despite it being his backfield, Chicago’s RB1 is facing one of the league’s top run defenses tonight. Seattle is second in yards per carry allowed (3.5) this season and has held 5 of 7 opponents under 100 total rushing yards. Right now, the Seahawks rank first in yards per play allowed (4.0) and are top-10 in turnover rate at 12.7%. Caleb Williams is going to have to live up to his “Superman” moniker and deliver with his legs and arm in Seattle tonight. Swift has gone under 60 rushing yards in 3 of his previous 4 appearances for the Bears. Bet on Swift Under 59.5 Rushing Yards at -115 odds. Zach Charbonnet Anytime TD Scorer ( +125 ) Zach Charbonnet makes his 2026 debut for the Seahawks following his recovery from a torn ACL in his left knee suffered during last year’s Super Bowl run. The Seahawks RB1 may take some time to shake the rust off, but he’ll be able to split carries with rookie 1st-round draft pick Jadarian Price, as well as Emanuel Wilson in a crowded backfield. In 2025, Charbonnet was a touchdown machine. He scored 12 times, deployed frequently in the red zone to punch in drives with his physicality. The Bears have allowed 5 touchdowns to running backs this season. Chicago has been fairly stout, but it’s likely that the Seahawks make frequent red zone trips tonight with their elite passing attack led by Smith-Njigba. Charbonnet won’t be available in Anytime TD Scorer markets at plus odds for very long. Let’s take advantage and bet on Zach Charbonnet’s Anytime TD Scorer prop at +125 odds.
